title: Chapter 14: Wu Wan
paragraphs: After fumbling with the Needle Case for a while to figure out how to use it, Chen Mobai finally waited out the two-hour detention. At this point, I urge readers to remember our domain: sto55.com.
Without even waiting for the Soul-Waking Charm to sound, he flung open the door and strode out.
Outside, only the last group of unfortunate stragglers remained.
Chen Mobai didn't spot any familiar classmates, which suited him just fine—it saved him the trouble of greeting anyone. Slinging his backpack over his shoulder, he left the school without hesitation.
Instead of heading straight home, he used his student ID to take public transport to a large, comprehensive raw materials market in the city's eastern district.
Chen Mobai's mother worked at a Talisman Paper Factory. When he was younger, she used to bring him there to play for several years, making him intimately familiar with the factory's processes.

The owner was a Second-Tier Talisman Master who ran a talisman shop in the city. To cut costs, he'd established his own Talisman Component Factory. The large sheets of talisman paper Chen Mobai had been cutting were purchased by his mother at an internal discount.

Though small in scale, the Talisman Component Factory was fully equipped, capable of producing writing brushes, ink, paper, and inkstones. However, materials rarely used in talisman crafting, such as gold powder, were sourced externally.
If Chen Mobai remembered correctly, the shop that supplied gold powder to the Talisman Component Factory was located here.
Cultivators generally possessed excellent memories. After asking three people, Chen Mobai accurately located Wu Ji Gold Store nestled in a corner of the trading market.
"Welcome, esteemed guest. What can I assist you with?"
As Chen Mobai entered, a young cultivator behind the counter, who had been engrossed in a book, immediately stood up and greeted him with a smile.

"Do you purchase gold here?" Chen Mobai asked directly, getting straight to the point. Before coming, he had checked the latest gold prices published on the Immortal Sect Network and was prepared to accept a slight loss on the sale.

However, the young cultivator didn't try to lowball him. After taking the gold, he placed it on a specialized Magic Tool to measure its parameters. Then, he offered 843 Merit Points based on the market price.
"This gold is of decent quality. It seems to have been refined by a cultivator using Spiritual Power. Let's round it up to 850 Merit Points."
Chen Mobai was immediately impressed by the owner's fairness and nodded in agreement.

After the transaction, seeing the 850 Merit Points added to his account, Chen Mobai suppressed his excitement and prepared to leave. But then his eyes fell on the book the young cultivator had left on the counter:
Second-Tier Artifact Appraiser Exam: Practice Questions

"Boss, are you perhaps an Artifact Appraiser?" Chen Mobai asked curiously. It was common knowledge that the Immortal Sect's certification exams progressed sequentially, tier by tier. Since the young man was studying for the Second-Tier Artifact Appraiser exam, he must have already passed the First-Tier exam.
"The exam questions from two years ago were relatively simple. I barely scraped by," the young cultivator said modestly, then handed over a business card.
Proprietor of Wu Ji Gold Store
Immortal Sect Certified First-Tier Artifact Appraiser
Chen Mobai read the card with solemn respect.
Most of the Immortal Sect's hundred arts profession certifications were officially issued only after rigorous selection and examination.

A First-Tier Artifact Appraiser certification meant that the holder had mastered most of the knowledge required to appraise Magic Tools and artifacts below the Second-Tier level, qualifying them for registration and certification.
This seemingly young shop owner could now issue authentication certificates for all First-Tier Magic Tools, and the results would be recognized by all major trading markets.

"Master Wu," Chen Mobai said, "I happen to have a Magic Tool my ancestor obtained during the frontier wars. I found it while cleaning the old family estate during winter break. Due to its age, no one in the family remembers much about it. Could you help me appraise it?"

Chen Mobai retrieved the Needle Case from his satchel. Wu Wan's previously smiling face immediately turned serious. He first donned a pair of disposable, thin gloves from his cabinet before solemnly accepting the case.
"Sir, would you like a preliminary appraisal or an in-depth analysis of this Magic Tool?"
Wu Wan's words left Chen Mobai utterly bewildered.Shouldn't artifact appraisal be a straightforward, one-step process?
Realizing his client was a complete novice, Wu Wan patiently explained the three-tiered appraisal system:
First-Tier:Visual inspection to determine the Magic Tool's grade, materials, and forging techniques.
Second-Tier:Requires specialized instruments to measure the tool's remaining lifespan and detect any hidden defects.

Third-Tier:The most challenging tier, testing the Artifact Appraiser's skill most thoroughly. It requires reverse-engineering the tool's refinement methods to create or deduce a spell formula that could perfectly unleash its power.
Naturally, the appraisal fees increase with each tier.
"However," Wu Wan added, "for most Magic Tools, especially First-Tier ones, only the first-level appraisal is necessary."
After Wu Wan explained, Chen Mobai finally understood the intricacies involved.

First-Tier Magic Tools had limited value but dominated the market in terms of volume. Profit margins were razor-thin; except for truly exceptional pieces, most underwent only the first-level appraisal. Many shops, focused solely on sales, simply required a basic Artifact Appraiser's certification and refused to invest in thorough evaluations.
Chen Mobai inquired about the appraisal fee. As a newly certified Artifact Appraiser with limited experience and insufficient Merit Points, Wu Wan offered a lower rate.
"This Magic Tool is First-Tier Mid-Grade. I'll charge you 200 Merit Points for the appraisal."
After examining the Needle Case, Wu Wan had a rough idea of its grade and quoted a price that made Chen Mobai's heart ache.
That's enough to buy six Azure Arrow Talismans!
But when he recalled his stiff control over the Flying Needles and the dangers of the Water Abode in the Eastern Barrens, Chen Mobai gritted his teeth and agreed.
With the price settled, Wu Wan placed the Needle Case on a workbench in the corner of the shop and began his appraisal, applying his professional expertise.
First, he measured the intensity of its Spiritual Power to determine its grade.
"The crafting technique is somewhat unconventional, but based on the overall Spiritual Power fluctuations and materials, classifying it as a First-Tier Mid-Grade Magic Tool is accurate."
Wu Wan then produced an Immortal Sect standard A4-sized certification card and filled in his assessment of the grade and materials in the designated spaces.
"The Needle Case was carved from a single piece of Lodestone. To determine the specific type of Lodestone and its origin, a second-level appraisal would be required."
Chen Mobai immediately shook his head. "That's unnecessary."

"The Flying Needles appear to be crafted from a mixture of metals highly reactive to magnetism. Even if you wanted a second-level appraisal, I wouldn't be able to assist you here, as it would require specialized equipment."
"This Magic Tool is quite ingenious, requiring only a minimal amount of Spiritual Power."
"The key to controlling this Needle Case lies in mastering its magnetic force. Once you can manipulate the magnetic field with precision, you'll be able to effortlessly control the Flying Needles."

Wu Wan, true to his reputation as a professional Artifact Appraiser, didn't even need to channel Spiritual Power. Relying solely on his extensive knowledge, he accurately described the crafting techniques and operational nuances of the Needle Case.

Chen Mobai felt a wave of embarrassment as he recalled how he had completely overlooked the Needle Case during his practice sessions in the school's Cultivation Chamber. He had treated it merely as a storage device, repeatedly forcing Spiritual Power into the Flying Needles, unaware of the proper method.
No wonder he had exhausted his Spiritual Power after only three minutes of operation. He had wrongly assumed it was due to insufficient cultivation.
It turned out his approach was fundamentally flawed. No wonder his efforts yielded so little progress.
